findings.title: Fixed-point C1 stripping can be forced into quadratic CPU work
findings.description: `top_path_log` is derived from an attacker-controlled diff header path and the new sanitizer repeatedly scans the whole string until no UTF-8 C1 pairs remain. Inputs like many `0xc2` bytes followed by many `0x9b` bytes create a new adjacent pair each pass, so convergence takes O(n) full-string passes, each doing 32 global replacements. A crafted oversized diff can make `prepare_content` spend excessive CPU before producing stderr.
findings.recommendation: Replace the fixed-point Bash substitution loop with a single linear byte-filter implementation, or cap the sanitized log path length before the loop and before repeated replacements.
findings.failure_mode: `top_path_log` is derived from an attacker-controlled diff header path and the new sanitizer repeatedly scans the whole string until no UTF-8 C1 pairs remain.

findings.description:
The diff splitter in prepare_content recognises only the bare `diff --git a/

b/

` header. Two attacker-reachable header shapes fail that regex: (a) git's default core.quotePath=true emits `diff --git "a/..." "b/..."` for any path containing a non-ASCII byte, a double quote, a backslash or a control character, which never matches `--git a/`; (b) with quoting off, a header carrying an invalid UTF-8 byte fails the match under a UTF-8 locale because glibc's `.` only accepts single-byte chars below 0x80 there — the new CMP-280 test comment documents exactly this ("under a UTF-8 locale the header regex's `.` does not match the invalid C2 C2 lead, so the path never reaches the strip"). An unrecognised header falls into the `else current_content+=...` branch, so the whole file's hunks are folded into the PRECEDING file's chunk and inherit its priority and its `is_excluded` verdict; if the unrecognised header is the first line of the diff, `current_file` is empty and the content is discarded outright when the next real header arrives (never in the manifest, never in the skipped list). A PR author who can make the diff exceed the token budget (any lockfile or generated file does) can therefore name a file `.claude/hooks/x".sh` preceded by `.about.md` (P3, or a `.reviewignore`d path), or `!x".sh` to sort first, and have a P0 hook change removed from the review payload while the summary names only the decoy.
findings.failure_mode: Review evasion: a security-critical file's diff is classified under another file's priority/scope or silently dropped, so the adversarial reviewer never sees the change and reports the diff clean.
findings.suggested_fix: Fail closed on header shapes the parser does not understand: match `^diff --git ("?)a/` and unquote git's C-style octal escapes for the quoted form (or run `git diff -z`/`-c core.quotePath=false` and parse under `LC_ALL=C`); treat any line starting with `diff --git ` that still does not yield a path as its own P0 chunk with the raw header as the name rather than appending it to the previous chunk; never discard pre-header content — emit it as a P0 chunk. Add a bats case for a quoted header and for an invalid-UTF-8 header under LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 asserting the file lands in the manifest at P0.
findings.demotion_reason: Demoted: anchor not in diff scope

findings.description: The stderr sanitiser hardened in this hunk strips C0/DEL and UTF-8 C1 only. Unicode format and bidi controls — U+202A–U+202E (E2 80 AA–AE), U+2066–U+2069 (E2 81 A6–A9), U+200B–U+200F (E2 80 8B–8F), U+FEFF — are valid UTF-8, so they pass the header regex in both locales, pass `tr -d '\000-\037\177'`, pass the C2 xx loop, and reach the `Top-priority file ${top_path_log} ... shown partially` / `listed as omitted` lines unchanged. There is also no length cap, so the line can be padded arbitrarily. A PR author can craft a path containing RLO/isolates so the operator-facing log names a different file than the one actually shown partially or omitted (Trojan Source reordering), hiding what SEC-001-style truncation dropped. The same changeset's CHANGELOG entry describes implement-gate's `strip_controls` as dropping C0, C1 and the Unicode format/bidi code points to a fixed point and cutting to 256 bytes (IG-13); this sanitiser, revised in the same round, lacks both.
findings.failure_mode: Log spoofing: the stderr audit line misrepresents which file was truncated or omitted, defeating the operator's only signal that the review payload was incomplete.
findings.suggested_fix: Reuse (or port) implement-gate's `strip_controls` for `top_path_log`: add the E2 80 8B–8F, E2 80 AA–AE, E2 81 A6–A9 and EF BB BF sequences to the fixed-point loop and cut the result to 256 bytes before logging. Extend CMP-279/280 with an RLO case asserting the sequence never reaches stderr.

findings.description: Raw 8-bit C1 bytes (0x80–0x9F without a C2 lead) are not removed: `tr` deletes only `\000-\037\177`, and the C1 loop targets the two-byte UTF-8 form. Under LC_ALL=C (the CI path the new test deliberately exercises) the header regex matches arbitrary bytes, so a path containing a bare 0x9B or 0x9D reaches stderr; the loop itself can also leave one behind (C2 9B 9B → 9B). Terminals or log viewers in 8-bit/ISO-2022 mode interpret 0x9B as CSI and 0x9D as OSC. UTF-8 terminals render these as U+FFFD, which is why this is a hardening gap rather than an immediate exploit.
findings.failure_mode: Terminal control injection into operator stderr on 8-bit-mode consoles; the sanitiser's stated contract ("stderr never gets a header's raw controls") does not hold.
findings.suggested_fix: After the C1 loop, verify the result is valid UTF-8 (`printf '%s' "$top_path_log" | iconv -f UTF-8 -t UTF-8 >/dev/null 2>&1`); on failure, replace every byte ≥0x80 with `?` (or `LC_ALL=C tr -c '[:print:]' '?'`). Add a CMP case feeding a bare 0x9B under LC_ALL=C and asserting it never reaches stderr.

findings.description: The new fixed-point loop runs 32 whole-string `${var//pat/}` substitutions per pass and needs one pass per nesting level; a header path of the form C2^k 9B^k forces k passes, i.e. O(32·k·n) work on attacker-controlled input with no length bound. Git's PATH_MAX-ish limit keeps a checked-out tree's names to a few KiB (seconds of CPU at worst), but a diff from `git diff <ref>..<ref>` or any non-git source has no such bound, and the loop runs before the budget cut. Termination is guaranteed (the string strictly shrinks), so this is a cost issue, not a hang.
findings.failure_mode: Unbounded CPU time in the review pipeline from a crafted diff header; the sanitiser's cost is set by the attacker rather than by the budget.
findings.suggested_fix: Cut `top_path_log` to a fixed byte length (256, matching strip_controls) BEFORE the loop, or replace the loop with a single O(n) pass that deletes `C2 [80-9F]` pairs with a stack (awk under LC_ALL=C), which yields the same fixed point.

findings.description: The test seam that lets AGENT_TYPES_FILE redirect WRITE_CAPABLE_AGENTS is gated only on BATS_TEST_FILENAME/BATS_VERSION being non-empty — two ordinary environment variables any caller can set (`BATS_VERSION=1 AGENT_TYPES_FILE=/tmp/x.yaml`). This diff changes only the comment, which now states that a hardened invocation runs the validator with a scrubbed environment, but no caller in the changeset performs that scrubbing (`env -i`, explicit allow-list), so the asserted mitigation is documentation rather than mechanics. Anyone who controls the validator's environment can make it accept skills that delegate writes to non-write-capable agents.
findings.failure_mode: The agent-type validation is bypassable by environment, and the written safety claim ("a hardened invocation runs the validator with a scrubbed environment") has no enforcing code behind it.
findings.suggested_fix: Either remove the env override outside tests entirely (tests pass the file via an explicit `--agent-types-file` argument), or have every production entry point (CI step, hook, `/loa` command) invoke the validator via `env -i PATH=... bash validate-skill-capabilities.sh` and add a test asserting the override is ignored when the markers are set outside bats (e.g. compare against a sentinel YAML).
